what: POSCO Holdings is South Korea's largest steelmaker and one of the biggest in the world. It also owns trading, engineering and battery materials businesses, including lithium and cathode material operations.
customers: Carmakers, shipbuilders, construction companies and appliance manufacturers in Korea and worldwide, plus battery makers.
money: carbon and stainless steel from Korean and overseas mills
moat: Integrated steel mills with among the lowest conversion costs in the world, supplying a domestic industrial base that buys locally.
risks: Net margin of about 1% as Chinese steel exports depress world prices
Revenue has fallen about 8% a year over three years
Battery materials investment has consumed cash with little profit so far
Only one analyst covers it in this data
opportunities: Analysts see large upside from the current price
Korean governance reform is pushing large groups to raise shareholder returns
Battery materials could become valuable if electric vehicle demand reaccelerates
watch: Steel spreads against Chinese imports and losses in battery materials.
